## Historical audit: S0265

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v2_4/results/task01/active/C1/selection/commons_31294395/trajectory.jsonl`. References below are JSONL lines; the supplied observations are complete lines, not split segments.

| Evidence | Observation and limits |
|---|---|
| Goal — line 1, student `model_request` | Reconstruct one indoor RGB photograph with separate SceneAct/Blender meshes and a matching camera. The intended semantic goal was visual fidelity, not merely a runnable program. The image itself is not visible in this audit. |
| Initial build — lines 3–5, student `model_response`, `execute`, `execution_result` | The student programmed multiple assets: room, windows, bed, two chairs, screen, tables, pictures and rugs. Bed rails, posts, mattress and pillows were grouped as children; this is evidence of assembly structure, not verified physical connection or support. The code specified a camera, three lights, fabric treatment and procedural wallpaper. Step 1 returned `ok: true` and saved a render; step 1 was selected at line 6. |
| Student review and revision — lines 7–10 | The student received the reference and first-render image inputs. Its revision ledger **claimed** the bed orientation was reversed, the armchair was too far right and frontal, windows and ceiling junction were too low/small, and wallpaper was absent on the right wall. It attributed the wallpaper issue to generic Blender primitive names and acknowledged nonunique camera attribution. These are student observations and diagnoses, not independent visual verification. |
| Executed changes — lines 9–10 | The complete second program rotated and moved the bed, turned, enlarged and moved the chair, widened the screen, changed camera target and lens from 36 to 40, altered lighting and wallpaper assignment, and replaced the table drape geometry. Several families changed together, so their separate visual effects cannot be isolated from this trace. |
| Validation and outcome — lines 11–12 | Step 2 returned `ok: true`, saved a render and was selected. This is **execution success**, not established visual or geometric success. No later student review, score, independent comparison, support check or collision check is recorded. Final image fidelity and whether changes improved or regressed individual regions remain unknown. |

**Teacher input and exploration.** No teacher event, teacher diagnosis or teacher-proposed update appears in the supplied trajectory; receipt or adoption of such input cannot be claimed. The student independently made a render-based revision, but no controlled intervention or separate diagnostic exploration is recorded. The general system instructions and runtime review request were available and received, as shown in lines 1 and 7; they are not evidence of a separate teacher interaction.

**Transferable lesson and uncertainty.** A successful render establishes that a build ran, while named parts and planned overlaps do not establish correct connections, pose, texture, framing or illumination. Simultaneously changing camera, objects, materials and lights makes attribution difficult. The particular bed orientation and wallpaper-name explanation are task-specific student hypotheses; without the actual images or further tests, neither their accuracy nor the final reconstruction’s correctness can be determined.
